FUNDRAISING & REGISTRATION

Fundraising and legal resources

NPO registration, incorporation as an NPC, SARS PBO approval and section 18A approval are separate processes. Use these official sources to adapt your stadgar to your structure and activities. The starting rules above do not automatically meet every registration or tax-approval condition.

  • DSD: registering an NPO ↗

    Official registration guidance, founding documents and reporting information for nonprofit organisations.

  • Nonprofit Organisations Act 71 of 1997 ↗

    The NPO governance and registration framework. The government page links to the amended Act.

  • Fund-raising Act 107 of 1978 — historical text ↗

    Parts were repealed by section 33 of the NPO Act. Read alongside later legislation; the original permit provisions are not a guide to current general requirements.

  • Fund-Raising Amendment Act 11 of 2023 ↗

    Later legislation concerning relief funds. Check applicable commencement notices and the current text before relying on an amendment.

  • SARS: public benefit organisations ↗

    PBO tax approval, qualifying activities and founding-document conditions. NPO registration alone does not confer this approval.

  • SARS: applying for income tax exemption ↗

    The application process for tax-exempt institutions and supporting documents.

  • SARS: section 18A donation receipts ↗

    Separate approval is needed to issue section 18A receipts, and qualifying donations and activities are restricted. A donation is not automatically tax deductible because its recipient is nonprofit.

  • CIPC: non-profit companies (NPCs) ↗

    Relevant if you choose the NPC company structure. Its Memorandum of Incorporation is a different founding document from an association’s stadgar; this template does not replace it.

  • National Lotteries Commission: society lotteries ↗

    Read before using raffles, lotteries or chance-based prize schemes to raise money. Different types of schemes have different rules.

  • Information Regulator: POPIA guidance ↗

    Donor information, privacy and direct marketing, including requests for donations. Consult the direct-marketing guidance when planning outreach.

Prefigurasie

Prefiguratiewe politiek beteken dat ons nou al, in hoe ons saamwerk, die verhoudings en maniere van organiseer uitleef wat ons in die samelewing wil sien. Die maniere waarop ons werk, pas by wat ons wil bereik: mense neem vrywillig deel, maak saam besluite en hou mekaar verantwoordelik.

Hierdie konsep word as ’n de facto-voorbeeld aangebied: mense kan kies om die beginsels in hulle eie stadgar (grondwet of verenigingsreëls) en hulle daaglikse organisering te gebruik, aan te pas en verder te ontwikkel, nog voor dié voorgestelde raamwerk ooit wetlike erkenning in Suid-Afrika kry. Sy gesag as ’n gedeelde praktyk kom van die mense wat dit aanneem. Om dit aan te neem, maak nie die konsep ’n wet nie en vervang nie die wette wat reeds bestaan nie.

A FRAMEWORK FOR ASSOCIATION

The freedom
to organise.

A proposed South African law for voluntary associations, inspired by the Swedish tradition of ideella föreningar (voluntary / non-profit associations): collective purpose, member self-governance, and accountability from below.

STATUSDiscussion draft

This text is a proposal for consideration. It is not an Act of Parliament and has no legal force.

Read the proposed Act ↗
12 official languagesOne common frameworkOpen to participation
01 / THE IDEA

Association begins
with people.

People should be free to come together, establish shared purposes and determine how they govern themselves. The state should recognise that freedom rather than make ordinary voluntary association dependent on prior permission.

The proposal draws on Sweden's ideell förening (a voluntary / non-profit association) tradition while recognising South Africa's constitutional commitments to equality, dignity, freedom of association, multilingualism and participatory democracy.

Legal context

South Africa already recognises common-law voluntary associations, and the Nonprofit Organisations Act 71 of 1997 provides a voluntary NPO registration framework. This proposal is illustrative and would require legal drafting and harmonisation with existing law before any introduction to Parliament.

07 / PRIVACY & SOURCES

About this site.

Join requests: The server stores your name, email, optional organisation and reason, selected language project (where applicable), and submission date in a local restricted file. The operator must secure this server, define a retention period and provide a contact channel before public deployment. Data is not automatically emailed or shared. Requests are not approved automatically.

Preferences: A first-party cookie stores the selected theme, language order, voice and reading speed for up to 400 days (browsers may expire it earlier). No analytics or third-party tracking are included.

Prefiguration

Prefigurative politics means practising the relationships and ways of organising we want to see in society through how we act together now. Here, the means reflect the ends: voluntary participation, shared decision-making and accountability to one another.

This draft is offered as a de facto template: people can choose to use, adapt and develop its principles in their own stadgar and everyday organising before any future legislative recognition of this proposed framework in South Africa. Its authority as a shared practice comes from the people who adopt it. Adoption does not enact this draft or replace existing law.

FUNDRAISING & REGISTRATION

Fundraising and legal resources

NPO registration, incorporation as an NPC, SARS PBO approval and section 18A approval are separate processes. Use these official sources to adapt your stadgar to your structure and activities. The starting rules above do not automatically meet every registration or tax-approval condition.

  • DSD: registering an NPO ↗

    Official registration guidance, founding documents and reporting information for nonprofit organisations.

  • Nonprofit Organisations Act 71 of 1997 ↗

    The NPO governance and registration framework. The government page links to the amended Act.

  • Fund-raising Act 107 of 1978 — historical text ↗

    Parts were repealed by section 33 of the NPO Act. Read alongside later legislation; the original permit provisions are not a guide to current general requirements.

  • Fund-Raising Amendment Act 11 of 2023 ↗

    Later legislation concerning relief funds. Check applicable commencement notices and the current text before relying on an amendment.

  • SARS: public benefit organisations ↗

    PBO tax approval, qualifying activities and founding-document conditions. NPO registration alone does not confer this approval.

  • SARS: applying for income tax exemption ↗

    The application process for tax-exempt institutions and supporting documents.

  • SARS: section 18A donation receipts ↗

    Separate approval is needed to issue section 18A receipts, and qualifying donations and activities are restricted. A donation is not automatically tax deductible because its recipient is nonprofit.

  • CIPC: non-profit companies (NPCs) ↗

    Relevant if you choose the NPC company structure. Its Memorandum of Incorporation is a different founding document from an association’s stadgar; this template does not replace it.

  • National Lotteries Commission: society lotteries ↗

    Read before using raffles, lotteries or chance-based prize schemes to raise money. Different types of schemes have different rules.

  • Information Regulator: POPIA guidance ↗

    Donor information, privacy and direct marketing, including requests for donations. Consult the direct-marketing guidance when planning outreach.

YOUR INFORMATION · YOUR CHOICES

Privacy policy

Voluntary Associations: The Association Commons

Last reviewed: 17 October 2026. This policy describes the current site, version 0.0.1. It covers browsing, expressions of interest, language suggestions, document creation and accessibility preferences.

Draft — operator details still to be confirmed

The collection described below is implemented, but this notice is not ready for a public launch until the responsible party’s legal name, address, privacy contact and Information Officer details are supplied. Retention arrangements and account-specific hosting locations and transfer safeguards also need confirmation. No fictitious contact details or registration status are supplied here.

1. Who is responsible and how to contact us

The person or organisation deciding how this project uses personal information is the responsible party under South Africa’s Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA). The project name alone does not identify that legal person. The project does not currently claim registered NPO, PBO or section 18A status.

Responsible party’s legal name: pending confirmation. Physical or postal address: pending confirmation. Privacy email and Information Officer contact: pending confirmation. There is currently no dedicated privacy-request form or published project privacy email. Do not put identity documents or sensitive privacy requests into the interest form as a substitute. The Regulator’s independent complaint route is listed below.

2. Information supplied through the interest forms

When you submit a general or language-project expression of interest, the application receives your name, email address, optional organisation or community, optional explanation, and the consent checkbox. For a language project it also receives the selected project code. Name, email and the consent checkbox are required for the form to succeed; the other descriptive fields are optional. No law requires you to submit this form. You can browse and use the document tools without doing so.

The saved record contains your name, email, optional organisation and explanation, request type, project code where applicable, a random record identifier and submission time. The checkbox is checked by the server but is not stored as a separate consent-history record. Records are held in private hosted object storage; the application provides no public listing or public download of them. The brief About summary remains unchanged; this policy gives the current operational storage detail.

These details are used to consider and respond to your stated interest and coordinate requested participation. Submitting the form does not create membership. There is no automated acceptance, mailing-list enrolment or automatic email forwarding. A language project does not automatically receive a copy of your personal record merely because you selected it.

3. Language suggestions and public tallies

When you type a suggestion and submit it, your spelling is sent to this site for matching against a language-name registry. A request identifier and, if you confirm a match, the chosen language code are sent too. The saved suggestion contains the registered language code and name and the submission time; the request identifier forms part of its storage key to prevent duplicate counts on retries. The application does not save the typed spelling, name or email as part of the suggestion record.

Visitors can see language names and aggregate suggestion counts. Individual suggestion records, request identifiers and submission timestamps are not exposed by the public tally endpoint. Counts are not verified unique people. They should not be used to infer who supports a language or project.

For abuse prevention, the suggestion endpoint temporarily uses the connection IP address in an in-memory counter with an hour-long submission window. It does not write that IP address into the saved suggestion. Old counter entries are removed on later requests or when the server runtime resets; an idle runtime may retain an expired entry until that cleanup occurs. Hosting providers may separately process network records as described below.

4. Stadgar drafts and document downloads

While you edit, your draft is held in the page’s memory. The application does not autosave it to an account, database, browser local storage or session storage. Leaving or reloading the page can lose the draft. Names, purposes, optional locations, adoption records, signatories and any other information you enter may identify you or other people.

When you request PDF, Markdown or RTF from the builder, the current form values and document language are sent over HTTPS to this site’s export endpoint. The application processes them in memory and returns the requested file. It does not intentionally persist the draft, add it to the interest records or log the draft body. The application does not send the text to an AI model or a separate document-conversion service. Hosting infrastructure still handles the request; this is not a promise that no service provider can process it.

Downloading a regular content page sends its page address to the export endpoint, rather than a personal draft. Export responses are marked private and no-store. Files you save, share, print, synchronise or back up afterwards are under your control and any services you choose. Avoid putting another person’s unnecessary personal or sensitive details into a draft.

5. Cookies, preferences and the language heat map

The application sets first-party preference cookies automatically. It has no advertising tracker, third-party analytics script, individual advertising profile or cookie-consent manager. Functional preferences are not presented as consent to unrelated processing. Browsers send applicable cookies with requests to the same site, even though this application uses the preference values in the browser rather than writing them into its submission records.

association_edition_preferences: theme, language order, per-language integer click counts, chosen speech voice identifier and reading speed. Its requested lifetime is up to 400 days from a save, and it is renewed when preferences are saved, including on page visits. The browser may expire it sooner. Click counts shade and reorder your own language buttons; the application does not combine them into a central visitor analytics dataset. This cookie contains no form name or email and no separately generated visitor identifier.

association_prefiguration_seen_until: remembers a display expiry for up to 24 hours. association_prefiguration_week_until: remembers the optional close-for-one-week choice for seven days. Older visit-count and open-state cookies are removed during migration.

You can remove or block these cookies using your browser’s site-data settings. Preferences and collapsed-state choices may then reset. Removing cookies does not delete a form submission already stored on the server. Any hosting or account-authentication cookies are separate from these application cookies and are subject to the relevant provider’s notice.

6. Browser speech and accessibility

The reader uses your browser’s speech-synthesis interface. It reads the available voice names and language identifiers to populate the selector, and sends the passage you choose to the browser’s speech engine. Some voices are local and others may use a browser or operating-system provider’s online service. In the latter case that provider may receive the text, including draft text if you play your draft. Its processing depends on your device, selected voice and provider settings.

The application does not record microphone input or save generated speech recordings. It saves the chosen voice identifier and speed in the preference cookie. Pre-generated audio and signed-language media are not currently implemented. You can use the page without enabling speech.

7. Hosting, service providers and other recipients

The site is hosted through ChatGPT Sites, operated by OpenAI, and the current application uses Cloudflare Worker and private object-storage infrastructure. Providers necessarily handle network requests and may process IP addresses, requested addresses, browser or device headers, security events and service logs. The application itself does not add a general visitor log or analytics database. Provider log contents, retention and backup arrangements have not been independently confirmed for this account.

Access to project-held personal records is intended to be limited to authorised project administrators and service providers supporting hosting, storage, security and maintenance. Personal submissions are not covered by the public content/software licences and are excluded from the downloadable source archive. The application includes no sale of personal records, advertising-data feed, public member directory or automatic disclosure to other language projects. Any later additional recipient or purpose needs a lawful basis and an updated notice.

Platform sign-in or access controls may operate separately from the site’s forms. This application does not request or read a ChatGPT account profile. Account information processed by the platform is governed by its own arrangements. See OpenAI’s privacy policy, Cloudflare’s privacy policy and Sites privacy guidance. These provider notices do not replace the project’s own responsibilities.

8. Purposes and lawful grounds

Interest-form processing relies on the consent requested at submission, under POPIA section 11(1)(a). The identified legitimate interests for limited technical processing are delivering the site and requested exports, remembering functional choices, securing the service and preventing suggestion spam, subject to section 11(1)(f) and your applicable objection rights. The responsible party must assess necessity and impacts and confirm these grounds before public launch. Legal obligations may justify specific preservation or disclosure where applicable. Merely browsing is not blanket consent.

Contact details supplied for an expression of interest are not permission for donation appeals, unrelated newsletters or other direct marketing. The current site sends none automatically. Any future marketing process must meet POPIA’s applicable requirements, including section 69 for electronic direct marketing.

9. Retention and deletion

POPIA section 14 limits retention to a justified period and permits specified exceptions. Relevant factors include whether the requested participation is still being considered, whether correspondence is needed, and whether a specific legal obligation or dispute requires preservation.

Current implementation: there is no automatic expiry or deletion job for interest or language-suggestion records. They remain in private storage until an authorised administrator deletes them. No maximum period, review timetable or backup-deletion interval has yet been confirmed. Those operational arrangements must be settled before public collection, rather than treating indefinite storage as the policy. Unneeded identifiable records should then be deleted or effectively de-identified, with any legally necessary retained copy restricted to its justified purpose.

Draft exports are processed temporarily in request memory and are not intentionally stored by the application. IP-based suggestion counters and cookies have the windows described above. Hosting logs, account data and provider backups follow separately confirmed provider arrangements; this notice does not promise immediate erasure from infrastructure the application does not control. Aggregate language counts may be kept after they no longer identify anyone.

10. Security and security incidents

Implemented application controls include HTTPS access, private record storage, server-side validation and request-size limits, same-origin checks for submitted forms, a hidden spam field, a basic suggestion rate limit, and no public route for personal submissions. These measures do not establish complete security: administrator access, account protection, provider contracts, backup controls and operational monitoring must also be maintained. Avoid sensitive details that are not necessary for your request.

If a qualifying security compromise occurs, POPIA section 22 requires notification to the Information Regulator and affected people as soon as reasonably possible, subject to statutory exceptions and permitted delay. Incident investigation should preserve necessary evidence while limiting further access.

11. International processing

Global hosting, storage, support or an online speech provider may process information outside South Africa. This account’s storage region, recipient countries and contractual transfer safeguards have not yet been verified; this policy does not claim South African-only hosting or an executed transfer agreement. Before public collection, the responsible party must verify recipients and establish an applicable POPIA section 72 transfer ground and appropriate safeguards. Choosing a language is not consent to an unspecified international transfer.

12. Sensitive information, children and decisions

The forms do not request identity numbers, health records, racial or ethnic information, religious beliefs, political persuasion, trade-union membership, criminal history or biometric data. Free text or an association’s stated purpose could nevertheless disclose sensitive information. The ordinary interest checkbox does not authorise every category of special personal information; POPIA sections 26–33 require an applicable authorisation.

No child-specific consent or verification process is configured. Before knowingly collecting a child’s information, the responsible party must establish an applicable basis under POPIA sections 34–35. Until appropriate arrangements are confirmed, do not submit a child’s identifying details through these forms.

Language-name matching suggests registered names; uncertain matches require your confirmation. Spam checks and rate limits can reject a request but do not decide membership. The application does not make automated membership decisions or build a profile for legal or similarly significant decisions.

13. Your rights and how to exercise them

Subject to the applicable legal conditions, you can ask whether personal information is held about you, request access, seek correction, request deletion of information that is inaccurate or no longer lawfully retained, and request restriction where appropriate. You can withdraw consent for future consent-based processing or object on applicable grounds. Withdrawal does not make earlier lawful processing unlawful. Some records may need to be retained for a specific lawful reason; a refusal should explain that reason and available recourse.

The project privacy contact is still pending, so an effective project request route must be published before public launch. Once available, identify the form or project, approximate submission date and the email used; provide only proportionate evidence needed to verify your request. Do not send an identity-document copy unless a justified verification process requires it. Browser cookies can be removed locally without identifying yourself. Anonymous suggestion counts may not be traceable to you without your request identifier.

The Information Regulator provides POPIA request forms, including objection and correction/deletion forms. Access to records may also involve PAIA where applicable; any required manual and Information Officer arrangements must be confirmed for the responsible party.

14. Complaints, external links and changes

You can raise concerns with the project once its contact channel is published, and you may independently complain to South Africa’s Information Regulator. Use its current complaints instructions and eServices portal. General enquiries: enquiries@inforegulator.org.za, 010 023 5200. Current contact information is available on the Regulator’s contact page. You do not waive complaint rights by using this site.

External legislation, licence and other resource links take you to separate sites with their own privacy practices. No payment method is currently provided, and this application does not collect card or bank-account details for donations. Before a payment provider, mailing list, analytics tool, new data-sharing arrangement or other collection is introduced, this policy and any necessary choices must be updated.

Changes will be dated here. A policy update does not automatically authorise a new incompatible use of information previously collected. Additional notices or consent will be provided where required. The site’s displayed release number remains 0.0.1 unless its owner explicitly changes it.

15. Legal and operational references

This policy is framed around South African POPIA, including sections 9–14, 18–25, 26–35, 55, 69, 71–72 and 74. Other laws may apply where the responsible party or visitors are located; this notice does not claim universal legal compliance. Official sources and the implementation facts above should guide the operator’s final review.

Prefiguration

Prefigurativ politik innebär att vi genom hur vi handlar tillsammans redan nu praktiserar de relationer och organisationsformer vi vill se i samhället. Här återspeglar medlen målen: frivilligt deltagande, gemensamt beslutsfattande och ömsesidigt ansvarsutkrävande.

Detta utkast erbjuds som en mall i praktiken, de facto: människor kan välja att använda, anpassa och utveckla dess principer i sina egna stadgar och i sitt vardagliga organiserande före ett eventuellt framtida erkännande av detta föreslagna ramverk i sydafrikansk lagstiftning. Dess auktoritet som gemensam praxis kommer från de människor som väljer att tillämpa det. Att använda utkastet gör det inte till lag och ersätter inte gällande rätt.

INSAMLING OCH REGISTRERING

Insamling och rättsliga källor

NPO-registrering, bildande av ett NPC-bolag, SARS godkännande som PBO och godkännande enligt paragraf 18A är separata förfaranden. Använd dessa officiella källor för att anpassa era stadgar till er struktur och verksamhet. Utgångsreglerna ovan uppfyller inte automatiskt alla villkor för registrering eller skattegodkännande.

  • DSD: registrera en ideell organisation ↗

    Officiell vägledning om registrering, grundläggande dokument och rapportering för ideella organisationer.

  • Nonprofit Organisations Act 71 of 1997 ↗

    Ramverket för ideella organisationers styrning och registrering. Regeringens sida länkar till den ändrade lagen.

  • Fund-raising Act 107 of 1978 — historisk text ↗

    Delar upphävdes genom paragraf 33 i NPO-lagen. Läs tillsammans med senare lagstiftning; de ursprungliga tillståndsreglerna beskriver inte dagens allmänna krav.

  • Fund-Raising Amendment Act 11 of 2023 ↗

    Senare lagstiftning om hjälpfonder. Kontrollera tillämpliga ikraftträdandebesked och aktuell lagtext innan en ändring läggs till grund för beslut.

  • SARS: allmännyttiga organisationer ↗

    Skattegodkännande som PBO, kvalificerande verksamhet och krav på grundläggande dokument. NPO-registrering ger inte i sig detta godkännande.

  • SARS: ansöka om befrielse från inkomstskatt ↗

    Ansökningsförfarandet för skattebefriade organisationer och de handlingar som behövs.

  • SARS: donationskvitton enligt paragraf 18A ↗

    Ett särskilt godkännande krävs för att utfärda kvitton enligt paragraf 18A, och vilka donationer och verksamheter som omfattas är begränsat. En donation blir inte automatiskt avdragsgill för att mottagaren är ideell.

  • CIPC: icke vinstdrivande bolag (NPC) ↗

    Relevant om ni väljer bolagsformen NPC. Dess Memorandum of Incorporation är ett annat grundläggande dokument än en förenings stadgar; denna mall ersätter det inte.

  • National Lotteries Commission: föreningslotterier ↗

    Läs innan lotterier eller andra slumpbaserade pristävlingar används för att samla in pengar. Olika typer av arrangemang har olika regler.

  • Information Regulator: vägledning om POPIA ↗

    Givarinformation, integritet och direktmarknadsföring, inklusive förfrågningar om donationer. Läs vägledningen om direktmarknadsföring när ni planerar kontakt med givare.

Friheten

Ett förslag till sydafrikansk lag om ideella föreningar, inspirerat av den svenska traditionen av ideella föreningar (frivilliga / icke vinstdrivande föreningar): gemensamt ändamål, medlemmarnas självbestämmande och ansvarsutkrävande underifrån.

Föreningslivet börjar
med människor.

FUNDRAISING & REGISTRATION

Fundraising and legal resources

NPO registration, incorporation as an NPC, SARS PBO approval and section 18A approval are separate processes. Use these official sources to adapt your stadgar to your structure and activities. The starting rules above do not automatically meet every registration or tax-approval condition.

  • DSD: registering an NPO ↗

    Official registration guidance, founding documents and reporting information for nonprofit organisations.

  • Nonprofit Organisations Act 71 of 1997 ↗

    The NPO governance and registration framework. The government page links to the amended Act.

  • Fund-raising Act 107 of 1978 — historical text ↗

    Parts were repealed by section 33 of the NPO Act. Read alongside later legislation; the original permit provisions are not a guide to current general requirements.

  • Fund-Raising Amendment Act 11 of 2023 ↗

    Later legislation concerning relief funds. Check applicable commencement notices and the current text before relying on an amendment.

  • SARS: public benefit organisations ↗

    PBO tax approval, qualifying activities and founding-document conditions. NPO registration alone does not confer this approval.

  • SARS: applying for income tax exemption ↗

    The application process for tax-exempt institutions and supporting documents.

  • SARS: section 18A donation receipts ↗

    Separate approval is needed to issue section 18A receipts, and qualifying donations and activities are restricted. A donation is not automatically tax deductible because its recipient is nonprofit.

  • CIPC: non-profit companies (NPCs) ↗

    Relevant if you choose the NPC company structure. Its Memorandum of Incorporation is a different founding document from an association’s stadgar; this template does not replace it.

  • National Lotteries Commission: society lotteries ↗

    Read before using raffles, lotteries or chance-based prize schemes to raise money. Different types of schemes have different rules.

  • Information Regulator: POPIA guidance ↗

    Donor information, privacy and direct marketing, including requests for donations. Consult the direct-marketing guidance when planning outreach.

Ukwenza ikusasa libe khona manje

Ipolitiki yokwenza ikusasa libe khona manje isho ukwenza ubudlelwano nezindlela zokuhlela esifuna ukuzibona emphakathini ngendlela esisebenzisana ngayo manje. Izindlela zibonisa izinhloso: ukubamba iqhaza ngokuzithandela, ukuthatha izinqumo ngokuhlanganyela nokuphendulana ngezikwenzayo.

Lolu hlaka lunikezwa njengesibonelo esingasetshenziswa vele: abantu bangakhetha ukusebenzisa, ukuguqula nokuthuthukisa izimiso zalo kuma-stadgar abo (imithethosisekelo noma imithetho yenhlangano) nasekuhleleni kwansuku zonke ngaphambi kokuba lolu hlaka oluphakanyisiwe lwamukelwe umthetho waseNingizimu Afrika esikhathini esizayo. Igunya lalo njengomkhuba ohlanganyelwayo livela kubantu abalamukelayo. Ukulamukela akulwenzi lolu hlaka lube umthetho futhi akuthathi indawo yomthetho okhona.

strings.5bcbb30b931e7777609bd26d7b777849bb558473: Voluntary Associations: The Association Commons — A proposed South African law
strings.181fb3bc8ccfba26ce1997abf5b1f095e7e4c264: People may form, join, support or leave voluntary associations without a general requirement for prior state permission.
strings.5b0d5837251cfac1a896fd4f713e03e1ccf2a838: Members decide their shared purposes, internal arrangements and activities subject to constitutional rights and the law.
strings.33f87307d280c341d6bc4f29d51d9c08389d58c3: The constitution provides fair and meaningful routes for members to participate in decisions, elections and oversight.
strings.7c3a947f1711f1e0ab6da271ab0c42cd8061a5ad: The association acts for a declared common purpose; surplus resources advance that purpose instead of being distributed as profits.
strings.816546d3828aca94d623b5a9be997d4e9a442a10: Written rules establish membership rights, office-bearer powers, decisions, accountability, amendments and winding-up.
strings.5f7e1545308018717214b6dfd0a264fe3d586ac7: An eligible association may hold rights and incur obligations in its own name, separately from individual members.
strings.c21a6cfd171e1b7e72f99ad72f5890a984e2c130: Delegated decision-makers answer to members through reporting, scrutiny, review and fair procedures.
strings.cf2d2be9652aabdf8369f21f1a48fdafe6afd9f7: This proposed measure may be cited as the Voluntary Associations Act. It would commence on a date determined by law following enactment.
strings.f6074ae49f6b9606e8e946a6e3ee0a8e0bf8291a: The objects of this Act are to protect freedom of voluntary association; recognise self-governing, member-based organisations; and establish minimum guarantees of transparency, fairness and accountability. “Association” means a voluntary body of persons united by a lawful common purpose under a written constitution.
strings.cfe4771232247dbe10950d48613ebf1f936d52c8: Every person has the right, consistent with the Constitution, to establish, participate in and withdraw from an association. No general licence or prior approval is required merely to associate. Lawful, proportionate restrictions may apply where the Constitution permits them.
strings.d696e4395b281bcdc410ea67eaef184592269dd6: An association is constituted when two or more persons agree on a lawful common purpose, adopt written rules and identify representatives authorised to act for it. The law may prescribe additional conditions for conferral or recognition of separate juristic personality. Registration under another applicable Act remains subject to that Act.
strings.09abf50ea71da923c2826858cad598c016e4b7dc: The constitution must identify the association’s name, purposes, admission and withdrawal processes, member participation and voting arrangements, governing bodies, financial oversight, amendment procedures, conflict resolution and dissolution. The constitution is binding on the association and its members to the extent permitted by law.
strings.61a717475df80a870b1816a028fafd71e508cc59: Membership criteria and decisions must comply with applicable constitutional and statutory protections against unfair discrimination. Members are entitled to accessible notice, fair treatment and a meaningful opportunity to participate in decisions affecting their rights, subject to the constitution.
strings.f4ce4c52e15df8879f629230ed7a680471671b41: The members must have access to a general meeting or an equivalent participatory decision-making process, held at least annually unless a lawful exception applies. The constitution must prescribe notice, quorum, voting and the recording of decisions. Consensus processes may be used where provided for by the constitution.
strings.7af76cdb7b029ec17d0e75e270e5819a67b9f7c6: Members may elect or otherwise appoint a governing body in accordance with the constitution. Delegated powers must be defined and exercised for the association’s purposes. Representatives must act in good faith, disclose material conflicts of interest and report to members.
strings.e0f804995c875c5b12152299239ca3639a56cb84: An association must keep proportionate records of its decisions, income, expenditure and assets. It must provide an annual account to members and make provision for independent scrutiny appropriate to its scale and risk. Any stricter statutory accounting, reporting or audit duty continues to apply.
strings.b69d534e708c8709f6b8f4b74766e08c31bafc47: An association recognised as a juristic person may, subject to applicable law, acquire property, contract, sue and be sued in its own name. Members are not personally responsible merely because they are members; this does not exempt any person from liability imposed by law. Surplus assets and income must be used to advance the stated purpose, subject to lawful remuneration and reimbursements.
strings.9248c6adf63d8378453a9dbc9e1959eb4d2c05c6: A constitution may be amended only through its prescribed fair process. Dissolution must follow the constitution and applicable law, with remaining assets dealt with lawfully and consistently with the organisation’s non-distribution purposes. Members must have access to fair internal dispute-resolution processes and lawful external remedies.
strings.dfa6986255835ae12716f3d70e1108c30c5b7f40: Nothing in this proposed Act should be read as replacing the Constitution, the Nonprofit Organisations Act, tax legislation, the Protection of Personal Information Act or other applicable laws. Any enacted version would require express conflict, transitional and consequential-amendment provisions.

strings.c07dc2e4430a7ef7235424ca510af95725d11da3: Den som stöder föreningens ändamål och accepterar dessa stadgar kan bli medlem genom att meddela sekreteraren. Varje medlem har lika inflytande och en röst. En medlem kan när som helst lämna föreningen genom att meddela föreningen. Medlemskap och deltagande är frivilliga.
strings.c72e6371c866b9dfbe0d6ae94cf257201e47adef: There is no compulsory membership fee. Members may agree voluntary contributions at a general meeting. Any proposal to introduce a fee is circulated with the meeting notice and decided through the amendment procedure.
strings.f402ff8d30349d8c338a09283e85e87b67222c45: Det finns ingen obligatorisk medlemsavgift. Medlemmarna kan enas om frivilliga bidrag på ett föreningsmöte. Förslag om att införa en avgift skickas ut med kallelsen och beslutas enligt förfarandet för stadgeändringar.
strings.a99747b7f2a046f33ebd983dcdf4a8423d0ff936: Members first seek a mutually agreed conversation or mediation. Any proposed restriction or ending of another person’s membership requires written reasons, a reasonable opportunity to respond, and an impartial decision. The person can appeal to a general meeting, with initial decision-makers and anyone with a conflict of interest not taking part in deciding the appeal. Members agree an independent reviewer if an impartial internal appeal is not possible.
strings.c10a9798ffca0ef87bd95e6bfd746314abd2160d: Medlemmarna söker först ett gemensamt överenskommet samtal eller medling. Förslag om att begränsa eller avsluta någon annans medlemskap kräver skriftliga skäl, en rimlig möjlighet att bemöta dem och ett opartiskt beslut. Personen kan överklaga till ett föreningsmöte, där de ursprungliga beslutsfattarna och personer med intressekonflikter inte deltar i avgörandet. Medlemmarna enas om en oberoende granskare om ett opartiskt internt överklagande inte är möjligt.
strings.d5b1e8da1807147012fa864fcdc769493de4f724: An annual general meeting is held within six months of the financial year-end. Members receive the agenda and relevant documents at least 14 days beforehand, through their agreed contact channels. Two members can call for an additional general meeting, to be held within 28 days. Meetings may be in person, online or hybrid, with accessible ways for every member to participate.
strings.48fa7ff104ffe9b72c38563ce14939b1af4f10cf: Årsmöte hålls inom sex månader efter räkenskapsårets slut. Medlemmarna får dagordning och relevanta handlingar minst 14 dagar i förväg genom överenskomna kontaktvägar. Två medlemmar kan begära ett extra föreningsmöte som hålls inom 28 dagar. Möten kan hållas på plats, digitalt eller i hybridform, med tillgängliga sätt för varje medlem att delta.
strings.81d25ae203c82589745fed4d4e1e25011dc8e45f: At the start of each general or committee meeting, those attending appoint a minute taker and at least one other participating member of the relevant body as a minutes reviewer (justerare). The minute taker records attendance, decisions, voting results and any dissent requested for the record, and sends draft minutes to the reviewer within 14 days. The reviewer checks that the minutes accurately reflect the meeting and agrees any corrections with the minute taker. The minute taker and reviewer approve the corrected minutes by dated signatures or recorded electronic confirmation. Approved minutes are kept securely and made available to members. If they cannot agree on the record, the disputed wording is identified, the minutes remain marked as unapproved, and the issue is referred to the next meeting of the same body for resolution and subsequent approval. Approval confirms the accuracy of the record; it does not reopen or replace the meeting’s decisions.
strings.7e9d2c58121a23b8b69877cd2e62db59f6aedec4: I början av varje förenings- eller styrelsemöte utser de närvarande en protokollförare och minst en annan närvarande medlem i det aktuella organet till protokolljusterare (justerare). Protokollföraren dokumenterar närvaro, beslut, omröstningsresultat och reservationer som begärs antecknade, och skickar ett protokollsutkast till justeraren inom 14 dagar. Justeraren kontrollerar att protokollet korrekt återger mötet och kommer överens med protokollföraren om eventuella rättelser. Protokollföraren och justeraren godkänner det rättade protokollet genom daterade underskrifter eller dokumenterad elektronisk bekräftelse. Justerade protokoll förvaras säkert och görs tillgängliga för medlemmarna. Om de inte kan enas om protokollet anges den omtvistade formuleringen, protokollet fortsätter att vara märkt som ojusterat och frågan hänskjuts till nästa möte med samma organ för avgörande och därefter godkännande. Justeringen bekräftar att protokollet är korrekt; den omprövar eller ersätter inte mötets beslut.
strings.8060056d35d5baa1b507cd195024e0dd42dc062b: A general meeting can make decisions when at least half of all members, rounded up, and at least two members participate. If this quorum is not reached, discussion can continue but decisions wait for a newly notified meeting with the same quorum.
strings.e2923f603f2b162e07dc4e05fb584ddfbcfdf3c7: Ett föreningsmöte är beslutsfört när minst hälften av alla medlemmar, avrundat uppåt, och minst två medlemmar deltar. Om detta antal inte uppnås kan diskussionen fortsätta men beslut får vänta till ett nytt utlyst möte med samma krav på beslutsförhet.
strings.5430dfa8ad41b2bad612e1059f5e62aca2b2a6a8: Members seek agreement through discussion. If agreement is not reached, an ordinary proposal passes with more than half of votes cast. Abstentions are recorded but do not count as votes cast. A tied proposal does not pass. Elections use a secret ballot if any member requests one; a tied election is repeated after discussion. Amendments and dissolution use the separate thresholds below.
strings.5cf0c82c64b020780947d4d6f469356813d1cdb7: Medlemmarna söker enighet genom diskussion. Om enighet inte uppnås antas ett vanligt förslag med mer än hälften av de avgivna rösterna. Nedlagda röster dokumenteras men räknas inte som avgivna röster. Vid lika röstetal faller förslaget. Val sker med sluten omröstning om någon medlem begär det; vid lika röstetal genomförs ett nytt val efter diskussion. För stadgeändringar och upplösning gäller de särskilda kraven nedan.
strings.ebc1d2651070b5727878507920a7dc2700a0ecf6: Members elect three committee members at the annual general meeting for one-year terms, serving as convenor, secretary and treasurer. They coordinate meetings, keep records and manage finances within the members’ agreed budget and decisions. Two committee members form a quorum; a committee decision needs a majority and a tied proposal does not pass. They report to members and disclose conflicts of interest. Members retain final authority and can replace a committee member at a general meeting after 14 days’ notice and an opportunity for that person to respond. Vacancies are filled by member election.
strings.817f80adba46db58e0147f7c2b2bec82c7ccd367: Medlemmarna väljer tre styrelseledamöter vid årsmötet för ett år, med rollerna sammankallande, sekreterare och kassör. De samordnar möten, för protokoll och sköter ekonomin inom den budget och de beslut medlemmarna har enats om. Två ledamöter gör styrelsen beslutsför; beslut kräver majoritet och vid lika röstetal faller förslaget. De rapporterar till medlemmarna och redovisar intressekonflikter. Medlemmarna har den yttersta beslutanderätten och kan ersätta en ledamot vid ett föreningsmöte efter 14 dagars kallelse och möjlighet för personen att yttra sig. Vakanta platser tillsätts genom medlemsval.
strings.f0a99affe0c468ec3448e2af794ec60d158bbb44: The association is intended to have its own identity, property and obligations, separate from its members, and to continue despite changes in membership or elected roles. Members do not acquire personal ownership of its assets through membership. Within applicable law and member-approved decisions, it can receive funds, hold property and enter agreements to advance its purpose. These stadgar do not by themselves guarantee legal personality or any registration status.
strings.b10f1ab32c84a31bd3e0707d3e6b4caf72fbad6d: Föreningen är avsedd att ha en egen identitet, egendom och förpliktelser, skilda från medlemmarna, och att bestå trots förändringar i medlemskap eller valda roller. Medlemskap ger ingen personlig äganderätt till föreningens tillgångar. Inom tillämplig lag och medlemsbeslut kan föreningen ta emot medel, inneha egendom och ingå avtal för att främja sitt ändamål. Dessa stadgar garanterar inte i sig ställning som juridisk person eller någon registreringsstatus.
strings.5c8ef3069414502bdc4f91ef49303d40150c2caf: Income, assets and any surplus are used for the association’s purpose and are not distributed to members or office-bearers as profits. Reasonable payment for actual services and reimbursement of documented expenses are permitted when approved without the beneficiary taking part in the decision.
strings.95e76b67c3f78108da3ecc85cfd182df9e83b300: Inkomster, tillgångar och eventuella överskott används för föreningens ändamål och delas inte ut till medlemmar eller förtroendevalda som vinst. Rimlig ersättning för utfört arbete och ersättning för dokumenterade utgifter får ges när beslutet fattas utan att mottagaren deltar.
strings.23908edb0fe261c3c5159ebfcbf3a91b85c42813: Financial transactions use a bank account in the association’s name. Members appoint at least two authorised signatories, and two people approve each outgoing payment. The treasurer keeps receipts and an income-and-expenditure record, reports to members at least quarterly, and prepares annual accounts. The committee does not borrow or commit to spending outside the agreed budget without member approval.
strings.21750241b816c9ea1be610730fa033946dff4f14: Ekonomiska transaktioner sker via ett bankkonto i föreningens namn. Medlemmarna utser minst två firmatecknare och två personer godkänner varje utbetalning. strings.d18e0c60199c177fe7bfe39f139b5de6dec91334: Medlemmarna utser en granskare som inte ingår i styrelsen och inte har hanterat de transaktioner som granskas. Granskaren kontrollerar redovisningen och rapporterar till årsmötet. Ytterligare krav på bokföring, rapportering eller revision enligt tillämplig lag gäller fortfarande.
strings.be7d597161c8e41a8775c993983231f18ee6fc75: A proposed amendment is circulated in full to all members at least 14 days before a general meeting. It passes with at least two-thirds of votes cast at a quorate meeting. The revised text and adoption date are recorded and shared with every member. Changes remain subject to applicable law.
strings.9a4c4e39b65d8c1d86e5a9e5f76d8a949e542d65: Ett förslag till stadgeändring skickas i sin helhet till alla medlemmar minst 14 dagar före ett föreningsmöte. Det antas med minst två tredjedelar av de avgivna rösterna vid ett beslutsfört möte. Den ändrade texten och datumet för antagandet dokumenteras och delas med varje medlem. strings.ed34b74235f47e739d85efc107ded433b70dd2ae: A dissolution proposal is circulated to all members at least 21 days before a general meeting. It requires at least two-thirds of votes cast at a quorate meeting. Members appoint people to settle obligations, close accounts and retain required records. strings.217ff6c47907aae84b839f13225a6d72087bd5d1: Ett förslag om upplösning skickas till alla medlemmar minst 21 dagar före ett föreningsmöte. /privacy/.title: Privacy policy — Voluntary Associations: The Association Commons

blocks.text: Prefiguration

Prefigurative politics means practising the relationships and ways of organising we want to see in society through how we act together now. Here, the means reflect the ends: voluntary participation, shared decision-making and accountability to one another.

This draft is offered as a de facto template: people can choose to use, adapt and develop its principles in their own stadgar and everyday organising before any future legislative recognition of this proposed framework in South Africa. Its authority as a shared practice comes from the people who adopt it. Adoption does not enact this draft or replace existing law.
Privacy policy
Voluntary Associations: The Association Commons

Last reviewed: 17 October 2026. This policy describes the current site, version 0.0.1. It covers browsing, expressions of interest, language suggestions, document creation and accessibility preferences.
Draft — operator details still to be confirmed

The collection described below is implemented, but this notice is not ready for a public launch until the responsible party’s legal name, address, privacy contact and Information Officer details are supplied. Retention arrangements and account-specific hosting locations and transfer safeguards also need confirmation. No fictitious contact details or registration status are supplied here.
1. Who is responsible and how to contact us

The person or organisation deciding how this project uses personal information is the responsible party under South Africa’s Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA). The project name alone does not identify that legal person. The project does not currently claim registered NPO, PBO or section 18A status.

Responsible party’s legal name: pending confirmation. Physical or postal address: pending confirmation. Privacy email and Information Officer contact: pending confirmation. There is currently no dedicated privacy-request form or published project privacy email. Do not put identity documents or sensitive privacy requests into the interest form as a substitute. The Regulator’s independent complaint route is listed below.
2. Information supplied through the interest forms

When you submit a general or language-project expression of interest, the application receives your name, email address, optional organisation or community, optional explanation, and the consent checkbox. For a language project it also receives the selected project code. Name, email and the consent checkbox are required for the form to succeed; the other descriptive fields are optional. No law requires you to submit this form. You can browse and use the document tools without doing so.

The saved record contains your name, email, optional organisation and explanation, request type, project code where applicable, a random record identifier and submission time. The checkbox is checked by the server but is not stored as a separate consent-history record. Records are held in private hosted object storage; the application provides no public listing or public download of them. The brief About summary remains unchanged; this policy gives the current operational storage detail.

These details are used to consider and respond to your stated interest and coordinate requested participation. Submitting the form does not create membership. There is no automated acceptance, mailing-list enrolment or automatic email forwarding. A language project does not automatically receive a copy of your personal record merely because you selected it.
3. Language suggestions and public tallies

When you type a suggestion and submit it, your spelling is sent to this site for matching against a language-name registry. A request identifier and, if you confirm a match, the chosen language code are sent too. The saved suggestion contains the registered language code and name and the submission time; the request identifier forms part of its storage key to prevent duplicate counts on retries. The application does not save the typed spelling, name or email as part of the suggestion record.

Visitors can see language names and aggregate suggestion counts. Individual suggestion records, request identifiers and submission timestamps are not exposed by the public tally endpoint. Counts are not verified unique people. They should not be used to infer who supports a language or project.

For abuse prevention, the suggestion endpoint temporarily uses the connection IP address in an in-memory counter with an hour-long submission window. It does not write that IP address into the saved suggestion. Old counter entries are removed on later requests or when the server runtime resets; an idle runtime may retain an expired entry until that cleanup occurs. Hosting providers may separately process network records as described below.
4. Stadgar drafts and document downloads

While you edit, your draft is held in the page’s memory. The application does not autosave it to an account, database, browser local storage or session storage. Leaving or reloading the page can lose the draft. Names, purposes, optional locations, adoption records, signatories and any other information you enter may identify you or other people.

When you request PDF, Markdown or RTF from the builder, the current form values and document language are sent over HTTPS to this site’s export endpoint. The application processes them in memory and returns the requested file. It does not intentionally persist the draft, add it to the interest records or log the draft body. The application does not send the text to an AI model or a separate document-conversion service. Hosting infrastructure still handles the request; this is not a promise that no service provider can process it.

Downloading a regular content page sends its page address to the export endpoint, rather than a personal draft. Export responses are marked private and no-store. Files you save, share, print, synchronise or back up afterwards are under your control and any services you choose. Avoid putting another person’s unnecessary personal or sensitive details into a draft.
5. Cookies, preferences and the language heat map

The application sets first-party preference cookies automatically. It has no advertising tracker, third-party analytics script, individual advertising profile or cookie-consent manager. Functional preferences are not presented as consent to unrelated processing. Browsers send applicable cookies with requests to the same site, even though this application uses the preference values in the browser rather than writing them into its submission records.

association_edition_preferences: theme, language order, per-language integer click counts, chosen speech voice identifier and reading speed. Its requested lifetime is up to 400 days from a save, and it is renewed when preferences are saved, including on page visits. The browser may expire it sooner. Click counts shade and reorder your own language buttons; the application does not combine them into a central visitor analytics dataset. This cookie contains no form name or email and no separately generated visitor identifier.

association_prefiguration_seen_until: remembers a display expiry for up to 24 hours. association_prefiguration_week_until: remembers the optional close-for-one-week choice for seven days. Older visit-count and open-state cookies are removed during migration.

You can remove or block these cookies using your browser’s site-data settings. Preferences and collapsed-state choices may then reset. Removing cookies does not delete a form submission already stored on the server. Any hosting or account-authentication cookies are separate from these application cookies and are subject to the relevant provider’s notice.
6. Browser speech and accessibility

The reader uses your browser’s speech-synthesis interface. It reads the available voice names and language identifiers to populate the selector, and sends the passage you choose to the browser’s speech engine. Some voices are local and others may use a browser or operating-system provider’s online service. In the latter case that provider may receive the text, including draft text if you play your draft. Its processing depends on your device, selected voice and provider settings.

The application does not record microphone input or save generated speech recordings. It saves the chosen voice identifier and speed in the preference cookie. Pre-generated audio and signed-language media are not currently implemented. You can use the page without enabling speech.
7. Hosting, service providers and other recipients

The site is hosted through ChatGPT Sites, operated by OpenAI, and the current application uses Cloudflare Worker and private object-storage infrastructure. Providers necessarily handle network requests and may process IP addresses, requested addresses, browser or device headers, security events and service logs. The application itself does not add a general visitor log or analytics database. Provider log contents, retention and backup arrangements have not been independently confirmed for this account.

Access to project-held personal records is intended to be limited to authorised project administrators and service providers supporting hosting, storage, security and maintenance. Personal submissions are not covered by the public content/software licences and are excluded from the downloadable source archive. The application includes no sale of personal records, advertising-data feed, public member directory or automatic disclosure to other language projects. Any later additional recipient or purpose needs a lawful basis and an updated notice.

Platform sign-in or access controls may operate separately from the site’s forms. This application does not request or read a ChatGPT account profile. Account information processed by the platform is governed by its own arrangements. See OpenAI’s privacy policy, Cloudflare’s privacy policy and Sites privacy guidance. These provider notices do not replace the project’s own responsibilities.
8. Purposes and lawful grounds

Interest-form processing relies on the consent requested at submission, under POPIA section 11(1)(a). The identified legitimate interests for limited technical processing are delivering the site and requested exports, remembering functional choices, securing the service and preventing suggestion spam, subject to section 11(1)(f) and your applicable objection rights. The responsible party must assess necessity and impacts and confirm these grounds before public launch. Legal obligations may justify specific preservation or disclosure where applicable. Merely browsing is not blanket consent.

Contact details supplied for an expression of interest are not permission for donation appeals, unrelated newsletters or other direct marketing. The current site sends none automatically. Any future marketing process must meet POPIA’s applicable requirements, including section 69 for electronic direct marketing.
9. Retention and deletion

POPIA section 14 limits retention to a justified period and permits specified exceptions. Relevant factors include whether the requested participation is still being considered, whether correspondence is needed, and whether a specific legal obligation or dispute requires preservation.

Current implementation: there is no automatic expiry or deletion job for interest or language-suggestion records. They remain in private storage until an authorised administrator deletes them. No maximum period, review timetable or backup-deletion interval has yet been confirmed. Those operational arrangements must be settled before public collection, rather than treating indefinite storage as the policy. Unneeded identifiable records should then be deleted or effectively de-identified, with any legally necessary retained copy restricted to its justified purpose.

Draft exports are processed temporarily in request memory and are not intentionally stored by the application. IP-based suggestion counters and cookies have the windows described above. Hosting logs, account data and provider backups follow separately confirmed provider arrangements; this notice does not promise immediate erasure from infrastructure the application does not control. Aggregate language counts may be kept after they no longer identify anyone.
10. Security and security incidents

Implemented application controls include HTTPS access, private record storage, server-side validation and request-size limits, same-origin checks for submitted forms, a hidden spam field, a basic suggestion rate limit, and no public route for personal submissions. These measures do not establish complete security: administrator access, account protection, provider contracts, backup controls and operational monitoring must also be maintained. Avoid sensitive details that are not necessary for your request.

If a qualifying security compromise occurs, POPIA section 22 requires notification to the Information Regulator and affected people as soon as reasonably possible, subject to statutory exceptions and permitted delay. Incident investigation should preserve necessary evidence while limiting further access.
11. International processing

Global hosting, storage, support or an online speech provider may process information outside South Africa. This account’s storage region, recipient countries and contractual transfer safeguards have not yet been verified; this policy does not claim South African-only hosting or an executed transfer agreement. Before public collection, the responsible party must verify recipients and establish an applicable POPIA section 72 transfer ground and appropriate safeguards. Choosing a language is not consent to an unspecified international transfer.
12. Sensitive information, children and decisions

The forms do not request identity numbers, health records, racial or ethnic information, religious beliefs, political persuasion, trade-union membership, criminal history or biometric data. Free text or an association’s stated purpose could nevertheless disclose sensitive information. The ordinary interest checkbox does not authorise every category of special personal information; POPIA sections 26–33 require an applicable authorisation.

No child-specific consent or verification process is configured. Before knowingly collecting a child’s information, the responsible party must establish an applicable basis under POPIA sections 34–35. Until appropriate arrangements are confirmed, do not submit a child’s identifying details through these forms.

Language-name matching suggests registered names; uncertain matches require your confirmation. Spam checks and rate limits can reject a request but do not decide membership. The application does not make automated membership decisions or build a profile for legal or similarly significant decisions.
13. Your rights and how to exercise them

Subject to the applicable legal conditions, you can ask whether personal information is held about you, request access, seek correction, request deletion of information that is inaccurate or no longer lawfully retained, and request restriction where appropriate. You can withdraw consent for future consent-based processing or object on applicable grounds. Withdrawal does not make earlier lawful processing unlawful. Some records may need to be retained for a specific lawful reason; a refusal should explain that reason and available recourse.

The project privacy contact is still pending, so an effective project request route must be published before public launch. Once available, identify the form or project, approximate submission date and the email used; provide only proportionate evidence needed to verify your request. Do not send an identity-document copy unless a justified verification process requires it. Browser cookies can be removed locally without identifying yourself. Anonymous suggestion counts may not be traceable to you without your request identifier.

The Information Regulator provides POPIA request forms, including objection and correction/deletion forms. Access to records may also involve PAIA where applicable; any required manual and Information Officer arrangements must be confirmed for the responsible party.
14. Complaints, external links and changes

You can raise concerns with the project once its contact channel is published, and you may independently complain to South Africa’s Information Regulator. Use its current complaints instructions and eServices portal. General enquiries: enquiries@inforegulator.org.za, 010 023 5200. Current contact information is available on the Regulator’s contact page. You do not waive complaint rights by using this site.

External legislation, licence and other resource links take you to separate sites with their own privacy practices. No payment method is currently provided, and this application does not collect card or bank-account details for donations. Before a payment provider, mailing list, analytics tool, new data-sharing arrangement or other collection is introduced, this policy and any necessary choices must be updated.

Changes will be dated here. A policy update does not automatically authorise a new incompatible use of information previously collected. Additional notices or consent will be provided where required. The site’s displayed release number remains 0.0.1 unless its owner explicitly changes it.
15. Legal and operational references

This policy is framed around South African POPIA, including sections 9–14, 18–25, 26–35, 55, 69, 71–72 and 74. Other laws may apply where the responsible party or visitors are located; this notice does not claim universal legal compliance. Official sources and the implementation facts above should guide the operator’s final review.

/en/.title: Voluntary Associations: The Association Commons — A proposed South African law

blocks.text: Prefiguration

Prefigurative politics means practising the relationships and ways of organising we want to see in society through how we act together now. Here, the means reflect the ends: voluntary participation, shared decision-making and accountability to one another.

This draft is offered as a de facto template: people can choose to use, adapt and develop its principles in their own stadgar and everyday organising before any future legislative recognition of this proposed framework in South Africa. Its authority as a shared practice comes from the people who adopt it. Adoption does not enact this draft or replace existing law.
The freedom to organise.

A proposed South African law for voluntary associations, inspired by the Swedish tradition of ideella föreningar (voluntary / non-profit associations): collective purpose, member self-governance, and accountability from below.
This text is a proposal for consideration. It is not an Act of Parliament and has no legal force.
Association begins with people.

People should be free to come together, establish shared purposes and determine how they govern themselves. The state should recognise that freedom rather than make ordinary voluntary association dependent on prior permission.

The proposal draws on Sweden's ideell förening (a voluntary / non-profit association) tradition while recognising South Africa's constitutional commitments to equality, dignity, freedom of association, multilingualism and participatory democracy.

South Africa already recognises common-law voluntary associations, and the Nonprofit Organisations Act 71 of 1997 provides a voluntary NPO registration framework. This proposal is illustrative and would require legal drafting and harmonisation with existing law before any introduction to Parliament.
Seven organising principles.
Freedom of association
föreningsfrihet — People may form, join, support or leave voluntary associations without a general requirement for prior state permission.
Collective self-governance
självbestämmande — Members decide their shared purposes, internal arrangements and activities subject to constitutional rights and the law.
Democratic member control
medlemsdemokrati — The constitution provides fair and meaningful routes for members to participate in decisions, elections and oversight.
Shared purpose
gemensamt ändamål — The association acts for a declared common purpose; surplus resources advance that purpose instead of being distributed as profits.
Constitutional governance
stadgar — Written rules establish membership rights, office-bearer powers, decisions, accountability, amendments and winding-up.
Separate legal personality
självständighet — An eligible association may hold rights and incur obligations in its own name, separately from individual members.
Accountability
ansvarsskyldighet — Delegated decision-makers answer to members through reporting, scrutiny, review and fair procedures.
Voluntary Associations Bill, 2026
Conceptual working draft · not enacted legislation
Short title and commencement
This proposed measure may be cited as the Voluntary Associations Act. It would commence on a date determined by law following enactment.
Purpose and interpretation

The objects of this Act are to protect freedom of voluntary association; recognise self-governing, member-based organisations; and establish minimum guarantees of transparency, fairness and accountability. “Association” means a voluntary body of persons united by a lawful common purpose under a written constitution.
Freedom to associate

Every person has the right, consistent with the Constitution, to establish, participate in and withdraw from an association. No general licence or prior approval is required merely to associate. Lawful, proportionate restrictions may apply where the Constitution permits them.
Establishment

An association is constituted when two or more persons agree on a lawful common purpose, adopt written rules and identify representatives authorised to act for it. The law may prescribe additional conditions for conferral or recognition of separate juristic personality. Registration under another applicable Act remains subject to that Act.
Constitution of an association

The constitution must identify the association’s name, purposes, admission and withdrawal processes, member participation and voting arrangements, governing bodies, financial oversight, amendment procedures, conflict resolution and dissolution. The constitution is binding on the association and its members to the extent permitted by law.
Members and equal participation

Membership criteria and decisions must comply with applicable constitutional and statutory protections against unfair discrimination. Members are entitled to accessible notice, fair treatment and a meaningful opportunity to participate in decisions affecting their rights, subject to the constitution.
General assembly

The members must have access to a general meeting or an equivalent participatory decision-making process, held at least annually unless a lawful exception applies. The constitution must prescribe notice, quorum, voting and the recording of decisions. Consensus processes may be used where provided for by the constitution.
Governing body and delegation

Members may elect or otherwise appoint a governing body in accordance with the constitution. Delegated powers must be defined and exercised for the association’s purposes. Representatives must act in good faith, disclose material conflicts of interest and report to members.
Accounts and oversight

An association must keep proportionate records of its decisions, income, expenditure and assets. It must provide an annual account to members and make provision for independent scrutiny appropriate to its scale and risk. Any stricter statutory accounting, reporting or audit duty continues to apply.
Property, obligations and non-distribution

An association recognised as a juristic person may, subject to applicable law, acquire property, contract, sue and be sued in its own name. Members are not personally responsible merely because they are members; this does not exempt any person from liability imposed by law. Surplus assets and income must be used to advance the stated purpose, subject to lawful remuneration and reimbursements.
Amendment, dissolution and disputes

A constitution may be amended only through its prescribed fair process. Dissolution must follow the constitution and applicable law, with remaining assets dealt with lawfully and consistently with the organisation’s non-distribution purposes. Members must have access to fair internal dispute-resolution processes and lawful external remedies.
Relationship to existing legislation

Nothing in this proposed Act should be read as replacing the Constitution, the Nonprofit Organisations Act, tax legislation, the Protection of Personal Information Act or other applicable laws. Any enacted version would require express conflict, transitional and consequential-amendment provisions.
How an association is governed.
Members
Form the collective basis of the association and exercise rights according to its constitution.
General meeting
The ordinary forum for major decisions, elections, reports and constitutional amendments.
Governing board
Implements decisions, manages resources and reports back to members.
Independent oversight
Members appoint reviewers or auditors appropriate to the size and risks of the association.
Constitution
Sets out purpose, membership, decision-making, representation and dissolution procedures.
Words worth keeping.
The original Swedish terminology is preserved to show the source tradition; the proposed law itself is South African.

/sv/.title: Voluntary Associations: The Association Commons — Ett förslag till sydafrikansk lag

blocks.text: Prefiguration

Prefigurativ politik innebär att vi genom hur vi handlar tillsammans redan nu praktiserar de relationer och organisationsformer vi vill se i samhället. Här återspeglar medlen målen: frivilligt deltagande, gemensamt beslutsfattande och ömsesidigt ansvarsutkrävande.

Detta utkast erbjuds som en mall i praktiken, de facto: människor kan välja att använda, anpassa och utveckla dess principer i sina egna stadgar och i sitt vardagliga organiserande före ett eventuellt framtida erkännande av detta föreslagna ramverk i sydafrikansk lagstiftning. Dess auktoritet som gemensam praxis kommer från de människor som väljer att tillämpa det. Att använda utkastet gör det inte till lag och ersätter inte gällande rätt.
Friheten att organisera sig.

Ett förslag till sydafrikansk lag om ideella föreningar, inspirerat av den svenska traditionen av ideella föreningar (frivilliga / icke vinstdrivande föreningar): gemensamt ändamål, medlemmarnas självbestämmande och ansvarsutkrävande underifrån.
Denna text är ett förslag att ta ställning till. Den är inte en lag antagen av parlamentet och saknar rättslig verkan.
Föreningslivet börjar med människor.

Människor bör fritt kunna gå samman, formulera gemensamma ändamål och bestämma hur de styr sig själva. Staten bör erkänna denna frihet i stället för att göra vanligt ideellt föreningsliv beroende av förhandstillstånd.

Förslaget bygger på Sveriges tradition av ideell förening (en frivillig / icke vinstdrivande förening) samtidigt som det erkänner Sydafrikas grundlagsfästa åtaganden om jämlikhet, värdighet, föreningsfrihet, flerspråkighet och deltagardemokrati.

Sydafrika erkänner redan ideella föreningar enligt common law, och lagen om ideella organisationer (Nonprofit Organisations Act 71 of 1997) tillhandahåller ett ramverk för frivillig registrering av ideella organisationer. Detta förslag är ett illustrativt exempel och skulle kräva lagteknisk beredning och anpassning till gällande rätt innan det kunde läggas fram för parlamentet.
Sju vägledande principer.
Föreningsfrihet
föreningsfrihet — Människor får bilda, gå med i, stödja eller lämna ideella föreningar utan något generellt krav på förhandstillstånd från staten.
Kollektivt självbestämmande
självbestämmande — Medlemmarna beslutar om sina gemensamma ändamål, interna förhållanden och verksamhet med iakttagande av grundlagsfästa rättigheter och lagen.
Demokratisk medlemsstyrning
medlemsdemokrati — Stadgarna ger medlemmarna rättvisa och meningsfulla möjligheter att delta i beslut, val och granskning.
Gemensamt ändamål
gemensamt ändamål — Föreningen verkar för ett uttalat gemensamt ändamål; överskott används för att främja detta ändamål i stället för att delas ut som vinst.
Stadgebunden förvaltning
stadgar — Skriftliga regler fastställer medlemmarnas rättigheter, förtroendevaldas befogenheter, beslutsfattande, ansvarsutkrävande, ändringar och avveckling.
Självständig rättskapacitet
självständighet — En förening som uppfyller kraven kan ha rättigheter och åta sig skyldigheter i eget namn, åtskilt från de enskilda medlemmarna.
Ansvarsutkrävande
ansvarsskyldighet — De som fått beslutsbefogenheter delegerade till sig ansvarar inför medlemmarna genom rapportering, granskning, prövning och rättvisa förfaranden.
